newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian journalists freed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian journalists freed in Chechnya.

text.p: Two journalists working for Public Russian Television who went missing in the breakaway region of Chechnya a month ago were freed on Tuesday, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Tass gave no details of where and how Roman Perevezentsev and Vyacheslav Tibelius had been released.
The two correspondents of the main Russian channel disappeared on January 19. Moscow and Chechen officials have been involved in talks but no details have been made public.

Russia's former security chief and likely presidential challenger Alexander Lebed, who is popular in Chechnya after signing a peace deal with separatist leaders last year, had vowed to help free the correspondents.

Kidnapping, usually for a ransom, is widespread in Chechnya where nearly every man is armed. The mountainous region was badly ravaged in a 21-month conflict between Russian troops and rebels which ended last August.
